content.heading: A little context.
content.description:
Early in my career, I thought the hardest part of software was choosing the right technology. A decade of building products and leading teams taught me to look closer: Who needs this? What are we assuming? What will be difficult to change?

Today I work with organizations navigating technical and human complexity. I write down decisions, make tradeoffs visible, and create space for the people closest to a problem to shape the answer. The work is part architecture, part research, and a great deal of listening.

items.subtitle: Case study · Platform strategy · 2025–2026
items.description: A growing engineering organization had a platform team, a roadmap, and very few repeat users. I led interviews with six product teams, mapped the recurring friction, and reframed the platform around a small set of dependable journeys. The result was a paved path teams could adopt incrementally, with ownership and feedback built into the operating model.

items.title: A migration that left room to learn
items.subtitle: Case study · Systems architecture · 2024
items.description: Rather than replace an aging service in one launch, we identified a seam, established a reversible routing layer, and moved one workflow at a time. This essay covers the decision record, the experiment that changed our plan, and why a clear rollback story mattered more than a perfect target diagram.
